newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Albanians desperate for lost pyramid money.
newsitem.headline: Albanians desperate for lost pyramid money.

text.p: Hundreds of out-of-pocket Albanians converged on pyramid company offices in Tirana on Tuesday, desperate to retrieve life savings they had deposited with the failing get-rich-quick schemes.

Crowds of up to 500 gathered at three offices. They waited with patience and pessimism at Vefa Holding, among the biggest operators, Sude, the latest bankruptcy, and Xhaferri, whose funds were frozen by the government last week.
"They are cheating us and we barely have enough money for bread," said a tearful middle-aged woman outside Xhaferri's headquarters. "Does (the government) know how we live?"
"Is our money lost? We are being kept in the dark and that is driving us crazy," said a young man.
On Sunday, thousands of investors staged demonstrations in Tirana and other major cities, blaming President Sali Berisha's conservative government for the loss of their savings.
Police broke up the protests and newspapers reported scores of arrests.

Sude's collapse provided a catalyst for the unrest. Last week the scheme's operator, 30-year-old gypsy woman Maksude Kadema, announced she had gone bankrupt leaving 50,000 clients bereft of around $50 million.
Western diplomats in Tirana said they were watching developments with concern.

"The government should find a way out not only to calm people but to help them get back at least to last year's financial situation. Otherwise it will have a lot of social problems," said one diplomat, who declined to be named.
Opposition leaders, who headed Sunday's demonstration, have pledged to continue their protests, termed illegal by the government.
Investors in the northern city of Shkoder said they would take to the streets on Thursday to demand the return of their money, Koha Jone daily reported.

Pyramid schemes boomed in Albania, Europe's poorest country, after the fall of communism in 1990, luring thousands of Albanians into selling their homes, land and livestock with promises of big returns.
